cards.q: What is the enterprise campus network?
cards.a: It is the full in-building/between-buildings network serving users, plus its server, WAN, and security modules. It is not one topology — it assembles three-tier hierarchy, star access, mesh-ish cores, and modules (server farm, WAN edge, wireless, DMZ) into a resilient, segmentable whole.

cards.q: Name the campus blocks and the topology flavor of each.
cards.a: Campus core is the routed mesh/collapsed backbone between buildings; distribution is a dual switch pair (HSRP) for per-building aggregation and policy; access is star for endpoints, VLANs, and wireless APs; server farm/DC uses spine-leaf (modern) or 3-tier; WAN edge is partial mesh/hub-spoke (MPLS/SD-WAN/Internet); DMZ is two-arm to firewalls for public-facing servers; management is a dedicated VLAN/VRF for OOB and NMS.

cards.q: What are the campus design goals (shared with Level 00)?
cards.a: High availability everywhere (dual core, dual dist, dual-home access, HSRP/VRRP, port channeling, redundant PSUs) to remove single points of failure; fast convergence via routed summaries, RSTP on L2, and first-hop redundancy; segmentation with VLANs per role plus VRF/ACL where security needs it (guest/voice/management separated); manageability via a dedicated management VLAN and OOB with NetFlow/telemetry feeding NMS/syslog; and QoS with trust boundaries at access, marking, and priority queuing on uplinks for voice/video.

cards.q: How is wireless treated in the modern campus?
cards.a: Wireless is a first-class citizen: APs connect to access switches and use CAPWAP to WLCs. SSIDs map to VLANs, roaming is anchored at the WLC, and AAA runs via RADIUS.

cards.q: In a classic small-campus scenario, what VLANs are typically defined?
cards.a: VLAN 10 users, VLAN 20 servers, VLAN 30 management, VLAN 40 voice, and VLAN 50 guest.

cards.q: What commands configure a distribution pair with HSRP and an access host port?
cards.a: On the distribution pair, configure 'interface Vlan10' with 'ip address 10.1.10.2 255.255.255.0', 'standby 1 ip 10.1.10.1', and 'standby 1 preempt'. On the access switch, use 'interface GigabitEthernet0/1' with 'switchport access vlan 10' and 'spanning-tree portfast'. The core is configured with 'ip cef' and OSPF area 0.

cards.q: Is the enterprise campus just a single-building star?
cards.a: No. 'Enterprise campus' is the whole modular model, not a single-building star.

cards.q: Where does the default gateway live in the campus, and where is STP used?
cards.a: The default gateway lives at the distribution layer (HSRP), not at the access switch. STP applies only to the L2 spans (access-to-distribution); the core is routed.

cards.q: How must you distinguish the campus core from the DC spine-leaf?
cards.a: The DC is often its own block attached to the campus core, so always distinguish the campus design from the DC spine-leaf.

cards.q: What is the common full-architecture answer for branch, campus, and DC?
cards.a: Collapsed core for the branch, three-tier for the campus, and a spine-leaf DC attached to the campus core.

cards.q: In the enterprise campus Quick Review, summarize each block's role and redundancy trick.
cards.a: Core is the backbone with dual routed switches; distribution does policy and routing with an HSRP/VRRP pair; access provides ports/endpoints with dual-homing and portfast; server farm supplies compute/storage with spine-leaf east-west capacity; WAN edge handles carriers/SD-WAN with partial mesh/DMVPN; DMZ hosts public services via two-arm firewalls; management provides OOB tools on a dedicated VLAN/VRF; wireless gives coverage and mobility with CAPWAP+WLC and SSID-to-VLAN mapping.
